title: Glock wins from pole as BMW dominate Oschersleben Race 1
dek: Timo Glock converted his first DTM pole into a win, 1.876 seconds clear of team-mate Bruno Spengler, as BMW took seven of the top eight places and Pascal Wehrlein took the points lead.

chapters.title: Lighter BMWs, a heavy Audi and a title race to settle
text: Oschersleben was the seventh of the nine race weekends of 2015 and staged races 13 and 14 of the 18. Mattias Ekström arrived as championship leader on 126 points, six clear of Pascal Wehrlein, who had led after Saturday in Moscow and lost the top spot again on Sunday. Edoardo Mortara was third on 110, Jamie Green fourth on 103 and Bruno Spengler fifth on 85.

Audi had won seven of the first twelve races, and the performance weights reflected it. At Oschersleben it meant the BMWs ran markedly lighter: Timo Glock's car was roughly 32 kg lighter than Ekström's Audi, the heaviest in the field, and even Wehrlein's Mercedes was only about 7.5 kg lighter than the Swede's. BMW was already quick in practice, and the weekend followed that script.

Dense fog delayed Saturday's schedule. The track is known for being hard to pass on, so grid position and the first corner carried extra weight, and the race was set at 40 minutes plus one lap. Glock came in with one previous DTM win and no pole position to his name.

chapters.title: Glock takes a first pole in a BMW top five
text: Glock set the pace in the twenty-minute session with a 1m19.821s lap, the first pole position of his DTM career. Augusto Farfus was 0.056 seconds behind in his BMW Team RBM car, and his team-mate Tom Blomqvist was third on 1m19.893s. António Félix da Costa and Spengler made it five BMWs on the first five places, with the whole top five covered by 0.106 seconds.

Wehrlein was the first non-BMW driver in sixth, 0.114 seconds off Glock,. Marco Wittmann and Martin Tomczyk took seventh and eighth, which put seven BMWs among the first eight. Miguel Molina was the best Audi in ninth, level with Tomczyk on 1m20.019s, and Mortara made up the top ten. Molina had slid into a barrier near the end of the session, but his car was repaired in time for the race.

The championship leader fared worst. Ekström could not get his Audi to shift properly on his final run and was left on 1m20.810s, last in qualifying; he lined up 23rd. Gary Paffett was 11th, Paul di Resta 15th, Robert Wickens 20th and Lucas Auer 23rd, and Wehrlein's sixth was the only Mercedes in the top ten.

chapters.title: Chaos at the first corner behind a clean BMW front
text: Glock kept the lead off the line and the five BMWs at the front got through turn one without damage, though Farfus dropped from second to fourth and Blomqvist from third to seventh. Behind them the field piled up. Mike Rockenfeller, Green, Wickens and Nico Müller were involved in the first-corner collision, and Mortara and Paffett were also caught up, with Paffett losing aerodynamic parts.

Debris on the track brought out the safety car. The race restarted, but a lap later the damaged bonnet of Wickens's Mercedes came off and the safety car was needed again, this time for a single lap. By the time racing properly resumed Spengler had already moved up to second behind his team-mate, and Ekström had gained several places from the back row.

The start-line incident set up the day's retirements. Wickens was the first out after four laps, Green followed after eight, Müller after thirteen and Paffett after fourteen, the Briton saying that bodywork damage and then a steering problem made the car very hard to drive. Rockenfeller was out after sixteen laps. Mortara kept going and finished 19th, six laps down.

chapters.title: No room to pass at Oschersleben
text: After the second restart the BMWs controlled the race. Spengler had passed Félix da Costa for second at the second restart and then settled behind Glock, who said he pushed to get out of the DRS window as soon as possible so that his team-mate could not threaten him. Félix da Costa was third, Farfus fourth, with little passing on a circuit where Wittmann and Martin both said overtaking was very hard.

Wehrlein ran fifth with the best of the non-BMW cars, but his power steering failed relatively early, just as he was putting pressure on Farfus. He kept his Mercedes there anyway and held off Wittmann, who was sixth and could not find a way by, a drive Mercedes DTM head Ulrich Fritz called a huge effort. Blomqvist and Tomczyk ran seventh and eighth, with Molina ninth and Daniel Juncadella tenth.

Further back Ekström climbed from the back of the grid to 14th but never got into the points. Maxime Martin, 11th, was the only BMW driver outside the points, and he said he had been compromised from qualifying onwards and had made contact with other cars at the first corner.

chapters.title: BMW MTEK one-two, Wehrlein takes the lead
text: Glock took the flag after 28 laps and 42m25.324s, 1.876 seconds ahead of Spengler, for a one-two for BMW Team MTEK. He also set the fastest lap, a 1m22.245s on lap 15. Félix da Costa was third, 7.881 seconds behind, and Farfus fourth at 10.051. Wehrlein took fifth, 12.734 seconds back, ahead of Wittmann, Blomqvist, Tomczyk, Molina and Juncadella.

Molina's ninth place meant that Audi scored only two points. Ekström finished 39.684 seconds off the lead in 14th. Wehrlein's fifth was enough to put him back at the top of the championship on 130 points, four ahead of Ekström, with Mortara on 110. Spengler's second place lifted him to 103, level with Green and 27 points off the lead.

facts.t: Glock's first pole becomes a win
facts.v: Timo Glock took his first DTM pole position with a 1m19.821s lap and led the whole race to claim his second DTM victory.

facts.t: Two safety cars at the start
facts.v: A first-corner collision and then the loss of Wickens's bonnet brought out the safety car twice in the opening laps.

one.label: Speedweek: DTM: Sieg für Timo Glock, Pascal Wehrlein Spitze

facts.v: Fifth place with a failing power steering gave Wehrlein 130 points and a four-point lead over Ekström.
BMW Team MTEK celebrated the first one-two in its DTM history, with Glock ahead of Spengler, and BMW's 67th DTM win.
